vector: Embeddings, metrics, ANN indexes and relevance testing
Explain similarity geometry and test a vector retrieval design
rag: BM25, chunking, fusion, reranking and grounded answers
Build an auditable hybrid retrieval pipeline
graphrag: Graph extraction, traversal, community search and evidence
context: Temporal context, decisions, agent memory and replay
Model provenance-rich context for AI workflows
agent: Tool routing, plans, permissions, and observable actions
production: Governance, freshness, metadata, benchmarking and deployment
Deploy retrieval systems with measurable controls

lessons.title: What an embedding represents
lessons.what: A text embedding is a learned numerical representation, not a bag of individual facts; neighboring vectors often correspond to similar meaning.
lessons.scenario: An enterprise service-desk assistant embeds approved incident descriptions and retrieves likely resolutions.
lessons.pitfall: A high cosine score does not prove that a passage is factually correct or authorized.
lessons.check: Contrast a paraphrased incident with an exact error code; compare both against a labelled relevance set.
lessons.build: Store model name, dimensions, normalization policy, input version and source-document ID.

lessons.title: Cosine similarity and geometry
lessons.what: Cosine divides the dot product by vector norms to compare directions. Identically directed nonzero vectors score 1, orthogonal vectors 0 and opposite vectors -1.
lessons.scenario: Rank short equipment-failure descriptions while document lengths vary.
lessons.pitfall: Zero vectors cannot be normalized; vector magnitude can be meaningful under some trained models.
lessons.check: Compute cosine for [1,0] vs [0,1], then [1,0] vs [2,0], and explain the rankings.
lessons.build: Implement a guard for zero norms and return stable tie ordering.

lessons.title: Dense versus sparse retrieval
lessons.what: Dense embeddings encode learned features across most coordinates; sparse representations emphasize a small number of lexical or learned term dimensions.
lessons.scenario: Search both a product description and an exact part number such as VALVE-742.
lessons.pitfall: Dense vectors can miss rare identifiers while sparse search misses paraphrased needs.
lessons.check: Create exact-identifier and paraphrase query sets and score precision for each retriever separately.
lessons.build: Maintain both a text index and embedding index with common document identifiers.

lessons.title: Dot product, normalization and distance
lessons.what: Dot product combines vector direction and magnitude; Euclidean distance measures geometric separation. Their rankings differ for non-normalized data.
lessons.scenario: Choose a similarity metric for an enterprise document-vector index.
lessons.pitfall: Changing the metric without changing index configuration makes historic similarity thresholds meaningless.
lessons.check: Rank [1,0], [2,0] against [1,0], and compare dot product, cosine and Euclidean distance.
lessons.build: Document index metric, embedding version, vector normalization and retraining migration.

lessons.title: Choosing and versioning embedding models
lessons.what: Embedding model selection must consider supported languages, input length, domain vocabulary, cost, latency, safety and query-document alignment.
lessons.scenario: Migrate a multilingual metadata glossary from one embedding model to another without losing result quality.
lessons.pitfall: Vectors created by unrelated models must not be compared as if they share a coordinate system.
lessons.check: Run a golden set in each required language; compare Recall@k, storage and rerank cost.
lessons.build: Use versioned indexes and dual-run comparisons before flipping traffic.

lessons.title: Approximate nearest neighbors and HNSW
lessons.what: Approximate nearest-neighbor indexes trade search speed and memory for imperfect nearest-neighbor recall; HNSW organizes navigable proximity layers.
lessons.scenario: Serve millions of enterprise asset descriptions under a strict latency budget.
lessons.pitfall: ANN top-k is not guaranteed to contain the exact mathematical nearest neighbors.
lessons.check: Compare ANN against exhaustive vector search on a held-out set; measure recall and p95 latency.
lessons.build: Tune index construction/query parameters; include periodic exact-search audits.

lessons.title: Vector index filtering and authorization
lessons.what: Metadata filters narrow candidates by tenant, classification, date and permission; the order of filtering and ANN retrieval affects both relevance and security.
lessons.scenario: A support engineer must only retrieve incidents for their assigned business unit.
lessons.pitfall: Post-filtering unauthorized hits can silently produce fewer results; missing filter enforcement can leak data.
lessons.check: Issue identical queries as two principals and prove disallowed documents never appear in evidence or traces.
lessons.build: Enforce ACLs before generation, validate tenant isolation and log filter decisions.

lessons.title: Multimodal vectors and representation alignment
lessons.what: Multimodal retrieval may align text, images and other signals into one shared or cross-linked embedding space; compatibility is model-dependent.
lessons.scenario: Find a machine manual diagram from a typed description of a pressure sensor.
lessons.pitfall: An ordinary text embedding does not automatically allow comparable image vectors.
lessons.check: Use labelled text-to-image queries and assess false matches on visually similar components.
lessons.build: Track modality, encoder version, captions, image rights and confidence separately.

lessons.title: RAG pipeline stages and boundaries
lessons.what: RAG separates ingestion, transformation, indexing, retrieval, ranking, context assembly and grounded generation. Failures can occur at any stage independently.
lessons.scenario: Answer an employee question from approved catalog policies without model fine-tuning.
lessons.pitfall: Good retrieval does not guarantee faithful generation; a fluent answer may ignore citations.
lessons.check: Trace one query from source file to selected chunks to final supported claims.
lessons.build: Define evidence IDs, retrieval version, budget and refusal behavior at every stage.

lessons.title: Chunking by structure and meaning
lessons.what: Chunk boundaries should respect section headings, tables, cross-references and paragraph semantics; fixed token windows are only a baseline.
lessons.scenario: Split a long supplier agreement into retrievable sections without detaching exceptions.
lessons.pitfall: A clause separated from its preceding heading can reverse its meaning.
lessons.check: Compare fixed, heading-aware and overlap chunking against clauses whose answer spans boundaries.
lessons.build: Store parent document, section path, page reference and offsets per chunk.

lessons.title: BM25 lexical retrieval
lessons.what: BM25 ranks passages with query-term occurrence, document-length normalization and inverse document frequency. It is valuable for rare exact tokens.
lessons.scenario: Retrieve a warranty statement by SKU, standard clause number or part code.
lessons.pitfall: BM25 may not retrieve semantic paraphrases with no shared meaningful terms.
lessons.check: Query for a precise serial code and a paraphrased user need; note different failure patterns.
lessons.build: Tune tokenization, field weighting and stopwords with representative queries.

lessons.title: Hybrid search and reciprocal rank fusion
lessons.what: Hybrid retrieval combines keyword and vector-ranked lists. RRF adds 1/(k+rank) for each list; it combines positions rather than incomparable raw scores.
lessons.scenario: Find supplier policy passages using natural-language intent plus specific contract references.
lessons.pitfall: Fusing poor retrievers can amplify noise; k in RRF is not the vector-neighbor count.
lessons.check: Calculate RRF by hand from two top-three lists and inspect ties and missing candidates.
lessons.build: Preserve component ranks in traces and evaluate fusion against single-retriever baselines.

lessons.title: Cross-encoder reranking
lessons.what: A reranker scores a query together with each candidate document and can improve precision, but introduces additional inference cost.
lessons.scenario: Retrieve 30 support passages and rerank the best 8 before assembling the prompt.
lessons.pitfall: Reranking cannot recover missing documents and may favor wording without authorization checks.
lessons.check: Compare Recall@20 pre-rank and nDCG@5 post-rank on the same query set.
lessons.build: Cap reranker batch size, set latency budgets and preserve document-level ACLs.

lessons.title: Contextual retrieval and parent context
lessons.what: Contextual retrieval can prepend a concise description of a chunk's surrounding document context before indexing, improving disambiguation.
lessons.scenario: A bare chunk says 'the threshold is 12'; its parent procedure identifies which machine and measurement.
lessons.pitfall: Generated context can introduce unsupported statements if not checked against the parent source.
lessons.check: Compare retrieval with and without parent title, section and verified context; audit additions.
lessons.build: Keep original text unchanged, attach contextual text separately and cite original offsets.

lessons.title: Query rewriting and multi-query search
lessons.what: Query transformations may expand acronyms, split compound questions or generate complementary subqueries, then reconcile their evidence.
lessons.scenario: 'Who owns C360 and what reports break if it changes?' requires ownership and lineage subquestions.
lessons.pitfall: Unconstrained rewriting can replace the user intent or remove exact identifiers.
lessons.check: Freeze a set of complex questions and compare original vs decomposed answer evidence.
lessons.build: Log original query, proposed rewrites, approved rewrites and results separately.

lessons.title: Evidence citations and answer faithfulness
lessons.what: A grounded answer should link each material claim to an accessible passage, provenance record or graph fact. Citation presence alone is insufficient.
lessons.scenario: Explain why a governed data product is delayed and cite the current approval ticket.
lessons.pitfall: A citation can refer to a page that does not support the claimed conclusion.
lessons.check: Have an evaluator inspect claim-to-passage entailment and deliberately test stale citations.
lessons.build: Require source IDs, revision timestamps and permission checks before returning citations.

lessons.title: RAG evaluation, recall and faithfulness
lessons.what: Retrieval Recall@k tests whether the evidence was found; answer accuracy and faithfulness test different downstream questions.
lessons.scenario: A metadata assistant must answer 30 approved questions with documented evidence and latency targets.
lessons.pitfall: An answer may be correct by coincidence even when retrieval failed; a high relevance score can still hallucinate.
lessons.check: Track recall@5, MRR, citation support and p95 latency on a reproducible split.
lessons.build: Version questions, expected evidence IDs, judged answers and retriever configurations.

lessons.title: Prompt injection and retrieval trust
lessons.what: Retrieved content is untrusted evidence, not instructions. The model must not execute embedded commands or reveal restricted context.
lessons.scenario: A malicious policy document instructs the assistant to ignore user permissions.
lessons.pitfall: If the system treats snippets as commands, a trusted workflow can be hijacked.
lessons.check: Inject a synthetic hostile passage and verify that only its subject matter is considered evidence.
lessons.build: Separate system instructions from retrieved data, allowlist tools and apply permissions at retrieval.

lessons.title: GraphRAG versus vector-only RAG
lessons.what: GraphRAG adds explicit entity/relation structure to retrieval; it does not require one storage technology or one universal retrieval algorithm.
lessons.scenario: Answer a question connecting a manufacturer, replacement component and impacted fleet.
lessons.pitfall: Pure similarity finds related paragraphs but might not recover a multi-hop dependency chain.
lessons.check: Measure evidence recall and explanation completeness against both vector-only and graph-assisted approaches.
lessons.build: Make graph traversals inspectable and always link relationships to evidence sources.

lessons.title: Entity and relationship extraction
lessons.what: Graph construction identifies mentions, canonical entities, relation types and source spans. Schema-guided extraction reduces type drift.
lessons.scenario: Extract supplier produces Component, installedIn Machine and ownedBy Site from maintenance records.
lessons.pitfall: An LLM may invent relationships not explicitly supported or confuse identical names.
lessons.check: For each extracted edge, verify a supporting span and an allowed predicate domain/range.
lessons.build: Keep asserted provenance separate from model suggestions and steward approvals.

lessons.title: Entity resolution and canonicalization
lessons.what: Entity resolution links aliases or duplicate mentions to stable IDs using constraints, matching signals and human stewardship.
lessons.scenario: Resolve 'North Works Ltd', 'N Works' and a source vendor code to one master supplier.
lessons.pitfall: A false positive merge can contaminate many downstream traversals.
lessons.check: Create hard negatives with near-identical names and different addresses; measure precision separately.
lessons.build: Store merge rationale, original identifiers, confidence and reversible mapping history.

lessons.title: Multi-hop graph retrieval
lessons.what: A multi-hop query follows typed edges across several entities, enabling relationship reasoning beyond single-passage similarity.
lessons.scenario: Trace Supplier→Component→Machine→MaintenancePlan to identify affected work orders.
lessons.pitfall: High-degree hubs can produce irrelevant walks; absence of a path is not proof of no relationship.
lessons.check: Restrict edge types and depth, then inspect every step against source records.
lessons.build: Use typed paths, per-hop limits, permission filtering and provenance for each edge.

lessons.title: Local search versus global search
lessons.what: Local search combines entity neighborhoods and supporting text for focused questions; global search analyzes synthesized community reports for corpus-wide themes.
lessons.scenario: Ask 'Which machine uses Valve-742?' versus 'What are the main failure themes across all sites?'
lessons.pitfall: Global aggregation can hide minority evidence; local search may miss corpus-wide patterns.
lessons.check: Build paired entity-specific and theme-level questions and score each retrieval route.
lessons.build: Route by question intent and label summaries as derived artifacts, not original documents.

lessons.title: Community detection and report hierarchies
lessons.what: Community-detection groups strongly connected entities; hierarchical summaries help broad exploration but require costly indexing.
lessons.scenario: Summarize recurring faults across industrial sites without reading every report in the prompt.
lessons.pitfall: Community labels and summaries may oversimplify sparse or conflicting evidence.
lessons.check: Compare summaries with raw events; ensure low-frequency critical failures remain findable.
lessons.build: Version extraction, partitioning, hierarchy and summary prompts together.

lessons.title: DRIFT search and adaptive expansion
lessons.what: DRIFT in Microsoft GraphRAG blends local detail with broader context through iterative query expansion.
lessons.scenario: A question about asset-replacement risk may require both specific installations and global reliability trends.
lessons.pitfall: Iterative expansion can increase token costs and drift away from the original question.
lessons.check: Measure evidence coverage, iterations, cost and topic adherence against local-only retrieval.
lessons.build: Set traversal/query budgets, preserve originating user intent and stop conditions.

lessons.title: Text-to-Cypher and query safety
lessons.what: Text-to-Cypher translates user language into structured graph queries; generated queries must be restricted to validated read-only access.
lessons.scenario: Ask 'Which active products depend on supplier X?' over a governed graph.
lessons.pitfall: Unconstrained generated Cypher can traverse unauthorized data or alter a database.
lessons.check: Use approved read-only patterns and test attempted writes, unbounded traversals and unknown labels.
lessons.build: Whitelist graph schema, set query limits and execute with read-only credentials.

lessons.title: Graph-grounded evidence and provenance
lessons.what: Graph edges must link back to the documents, records, timestamps and extraction decisions that justify them.
lessons.scenario: Show a supplier-to-asset dependency along with the purchase order and inspection record that support it.
lessons.pitfall: Treating every edge as equally trustworthy hides extraction and record-quality uncertainty.
lessons.check: Remove one supporting record and verify that the answer flags weakened or missing evidence.
lessons.build: Use PROV-O or equivalent provenance links with source offsets and version IDs.

lessons.title: GraphRAG benchmarking and ablation
lessons.what: Compare vector-only, lexical, hybrid and graph-assisted variants on identical questions, judged evidence and access rules.
lessons.scenario: Prove whether graph traversal improves dependency-analysis questions enough to justify indexing cost.
lessons.pitfall: Improving one curated query does not establish robust performance; leakage inflates scores.
lessons.check: Run ablations with graph off, reranker off and controlled entity-resolution noise.
lessons.build: Report question mix, relevance labels, recall, faithfulness, latency and infrastructure cost.

lessons.title: What is an enterprise context graph?
lessons.what: A context graph extends linked enterprise knowledge with operational state, decisions, workflow events and evidence relevant to an agent's actions; the term is emerging rather than a single fixed W3C standard.
lessons.scenario: An AI incident agent needs to know the current service owner, why a workaround was approved, and whether the approval expired.
lessons.pitfall: A static knowledge graph of assets alone may lack decision history and runtime state.
lessons.check: Compare one agent decision using only entity facts versus versioned workflow and approval context.
lessons.build: Model entities, events, decisions, policies, actors, time and sources separately.

lessons.title: Temporal knowledge and valid-time facts
lessons.what: Time-sensitive context distinguishes when a fact was true in the real world from when the system learned or recorded it.
lessons.scenario: A supplier was approved last quarter but suspended this morning.
lessons.pitfall: Using only the latest state loses the history needed to explain earlier decisions.
lessons.check: Ask 'What did we know on Tuesday?' versus 'What was valid on Tuesday?' and compare answers.
lessons.build: Store validFrom/validTo and recordedAt or equivalent bitemporal fields.

lessons.title: Decision provenance and approval rationale
lessons.what: A decision record should capture proposed action, constraints, evidence, reviewer, outcome and affected version.
lessons.scenario: An agent recommends a data-product release; a steward blocks it for failed validation.
lessons.pitfall: Without rationale, another agent cannot distinguish a policy exception from routine success.
lessons.check: Replay an old decision against its original policy and source snapshot.
lessons.build: Keep durable decision IDs and links to approving actor and policy version.

lessons.title: Agent memory versus knowledge graphs
lessons.what: Agent conversation memory records interactions and state; a knowledge graph represents reusable structured entities and relations. Both can interact but serve different needs.
lessons.scenario: An agent remembers a user's requested dashboard while querying approved business definitions from the graph.
lessons.pitfall: Copying raw chat history into a shared graph can expose private or obsolete preferences.
lessons.check: Test retention, deletion and cross-user isolation with synthetic histories.
lessons.build: Separate ephemeral session state, user preferences and authoritative enterprise facts.

lessons.title: Context assembly and token budgets
lessons.what: Context assembly selects the smallest sufficient relevant evidence from vector hits, graph paths, rules and recent events.
lessons.scenario: A policy assistant must answer within a strict token budget while retaining the decisive exception clause.
lessons.pitfall: Long context can dilute evidence; cutting out the exception yields a wrong confident answer.
lessons.check: Measure recall of critical citations as token budget shrinks; include an abstention case.
lessons.build: Rank evidence utility, deduplicate, include provenance and preserve permission filters.

lessons.title: Event-driven context updates
lessons.what: Enterprise context may change via CDC, workflow events and API updates; retrieval indexes and graph edges must indicate freshness.
lessons.scenario: A supplier's risk status changes while a procurement agent is drafting a decision.
lessons.pitfall: An old vector index can contradict the authoritative current record.
lessons.check: Send update/delete events and measure propagation and stale-read windows.
lessons.build: Track event IDs, idempotency, tombstones and index checkpoint status.

lessons.title: Context graph access governance
lessons.what: Context is often the most sensitive layer because it combines identities, decisions, incidents and access patterns.
lessons.scenario: An agent asks why a restricted contract was rejected, but lacks clearance for its legal clauses.
lessons.pitfall: Even a summary or graph path can reveal restricted relationships.
lessons.check: Run persona-separated tests and confirm forbidden edges never reach a prompt or explanation.
lessons.build: Apply policy to nodes, relationships, retrieved text and derived summaries.

lessons.title: Context graph validation and replay
lessons.what: Replay a recorded agent decision using the same facts, policy revision and context snapshot to assess reproducibility.
lessons.scenario: Investigate why a procurement assistant approved a request last month.
lessons.pitfall: Model drift, expired permissions or overwritten states can make old decisions impossible to reconstruct.
lessons.check: Pin context snapshot and tool versions, then compare proposed versus recorded decisions.
lessons.build: Store immutable event references, graph version, retrieval trace and decision output.

lessons.title: Agentic retrieval and question planning
lessons.what: An agentic retrieval workflow may plan subqueries, select evidence tools, inspect results and stop when evidence is sufficient.
lessons.scenario: An analyst asks a cross-system question spanning catalog ownership, change tickets and supplier risk.
lessons.pitfall: Unlimited self-directed searches waste time and may compound spurious evidence.
lessons.check: Set maximum tool calls, a coverage rubric and an explicit fallback for missing proof.
lessons.build: Log planner decisions and evaluate each tool choice against a fixed query set.

lessons.title: Tool routing across SQL, graph and vectors
lessons.what: A router chooses SQL for aggregates, graphs for paths, keyword search for IDs, and vector retrieval for paraphrases.
lessons.scenario: Answer 'Which five data products depend on this retired code, and who approved the change?'
lessons.pitfall: Using one tool for every subquestion creates avoidable errors or slow responses.
lessons.check: Label queries by ideal tool and measure routing accuracy plus total task success.
lessons.build: Keep a shared canonical entity ID and compatible permissions across tools.

lessons.title: Retrieval plans and query decomposition
lessons.what: Decomposing a question creates dependent subqueries whose evidence can be joined by entity ID and time.
lessons.scenario: First identify affected products, then join their owning stewards and approval records.
lessons.pitfall: Subqueries may disagree on time period or entity identity and yield inconsistent answers.
lessons.check: Execute plan against a synthetic changed-source scenario and inspect join keys.
lessons.build: Track query DAG, intermediate evidence, filters and query-level confidence.

lessons.title: Tool-output validation and schema contracts
lessons.what: Agent tool output must match typed schemas and distinguish evidence, uncertainty, errors and permission denials.
lessons.scenario: A graph traversal tool returns entities with canonical IDs, source citations and stale flags.
lessons.pitfall: Free-form output makes it easy to mistake an error message for factual evidence.
lessons.check: Fuzz missing fields, wrong types and empty paths; require explicit fallback handling.
lessons.build: Validate input and output JSON schemas and version contracts.

lessons.title: Human approval and reversible actions
lessons.what: High-impact actions require bounded automation, human approval and an audit trail that records policy and evidence.
lessons.scenario: An agent proposes merging duplicate customer masters but must not silently approve the merge.
lessons.pitfall: A wrong irreversible action can corrupt MDM identities at enterprise scale.
lessons.check: Test approve, reject, revoke and timeout paths; confirm no write without authorization.
lessons.build: Stage proposed changes, show semantic diff, sign approvals and support rollback.

lessons.title: Grounded planning and uncertainty
lessons.what: A planning agent should distinguish known facts, inferred implications, assumptions and unanswered questions.
lessons.scenario: An agent analyzes outage blast radius but two source systems disagree about ownership.
lessons.pitfall: Converting plausible guesses into authoritative graph edges causes escalating errors.
lessons.check: Test conflicting evidence and verify the system surfaces disagreement or abstains.
lessons.build: Carry evidence-level confidence with source IDs; never invent supporting citations.

lessons.title: Graph-based agent evaluation
lessons.what: Task benchmarks should evaluate tool-selection, evidence correctness, authorization, latency and completion—not only language fluency.
lessons.scenario: Evaluate an incident agent across 60 synthetic tickets, including adversarial inputs.
lessons.pitfall: A high tool-call success rate does not imply task correctness or safety.
lessons.check: Compare success on multi-hop queries and permission-restricted queries separately.
lessons.build: Version task scripts, tool fixtures, ground truth and outcome scoring.

lessons.title: Agent trace observability
lessons.what: Execution traces reveal query planning, retrieval stages, source access, reasoning steps exposed by tooling, and final citation support.
lessons.scenario: Investigate a wrong supplier-risk answer by identifying the first missing evidence hop.
lessons.pitfall: Logging raw secrets or private prompt context creates its own security incident.
lessons.check: Verify logs redact sensitive fields and still reconstruct a deterministic evaluation trace.
lessons.build: Record query IDs, document IDs, ranking factors, latency and policy decisions.

lessons.title: Reference architecture for enterprise RAG
lessons.what: A production architecture separates connectors, ingestion, identity, embeddings, graph, retrieval, reranking, generation and governance planes.
lessons.scenario: Combine ERP purchase orders, CRM customers, asset inventories and approved policies.
lessons.pitfall: A monolithic 'AI graph' with undefined owners and no replay capability becomes unmaintainable.
lessons.check: Trace a document deletion through graph, index, caches and generated evidence.
lessons.build: Specify data contract, SLO, service owner and lineage for every stage.

lessons.title: Metadata, lineage and retrieval provenance
lessons.what: Every retrieved chunk and graph edge should link to a catalog asset, source version, processing run and steward.
lessons.scenario: An auditor asks which version of a contract informed an agent decision.
lessons.pitfall: A copied chunk with no origin cannot support reliable citations or deletion requests.
lessons.check: Delete or replace a source and verify that all derived indexes receive the change.
lessons.build: Adopt DCAT/PROV-style descriptions and stable ingestion run IDs.

lessons.title: Index refresh, CDC and consistency
lessons.what: Ingestion pipelines need idempotent updates, tombstones, concurrency controls and explicit freshness guarantees.
lessons.scenario: A supplier status changes in ERP while its graph and vector index update asynchronously.
lessons.pitfall: Readers may see hybrid evidence from mismatched versions and make contradictory claims.
lessons.check: Inject delayed and duplicated change events; verify reprocessing and reconciliation.
lessons.build: Track source watermark, graph commit ID, vector index batch and refresh status.

lessons.title: PII minimization and permission-aware RAG
lessons.what: Personal data and privileged business information require source-level minimization and consistent retrieval ACL enforcement.
lessons.scenario: A manager's request must not surface a colleague's private review notes.
lessons.pitfall: Redacting only final generation still leaves sensitive text in indexes and traces.
lessons.check: Test unauthorized nearest-neighbor matches and access after role revocation.
lessons.build: Define classification, retention, purpose limitation and deletion across all derived stores.

lessons.title: Cost, latency and accuracy budgets
lessons.what: GraphRAG indexing, model calls, reranking and multi-hop traversals have different costs; design for measurable tradeoffs.
lessons.scenario: Decide if community summaries are justified for a frequently asked broad portfolio question.
lessons.pitfall: Optimizing only average latency hides expensive tail queries and poor global search cost.
lessons.check: Compare per-stage cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, Recall@k and factual support.
lessons.build: Apply query routing, caching and fallback based on benchmarked benefit.

lessons.title: Model and prompt version changes
lessons.what: Changes to embedding models, extractors, prompts or ontologies may alter rankings and graph edges even when source data is unchanged.
lessons.scenario: Roll out a new multilingual embedder to the supplier knowledge assistant.
lessons.pitfall: Mixed embedding dimensions or incompatible graph schemas cause silent failures or runtime errors.
lessons.check: Shadow-run new versions and compare trace-level evidence before cutover.
lessons.build: Use immutable manifest of model, tokenizer, schema, prompt, corpus and index versions.

lessons.title: GraphRAG deployment decision framework
lessons.what: Choose document RAG, hybrid retrieval or GraphRAG by question mix, relation complexity, freshness, privacy and operating cost.
lessons.scenario: A help-center FAQ uses hybrid RAG; supplier dependency impact analysis benefits from graph paths.
lessons.pitfall: A graph is not inherently better for every question and may add costly extraction errors.
lessons.check: Test matched baselines for single-document, aggregate, and multi-hop queries.
lessons.build: Justify graph construction only if measured outcomes outweigh upkeep cost.

lessons.title: Responsible use, licenses and evaluation governance
lessons.what: Evaluation corpora, third-party vocabularies, model weights and uploaded documents each have separate rights and obligations.
lessons.scenario: Publish an open enterprise AI demo using only fictional suppliers and legally reusable standards references.
lessons.pitfall: A permissive code license does not grant rights to redistribute vendor manuals or customer records.
lessons.check: Run a fixture inventory covering source, license, permissions, personal data and retention.
lessons.build: Document dataset provenance, licenses, test results and model limitations before release.
